## Goal
- Complete P0 IVX mobile stability work for cache-first modules, resilient media uploads, bounded Reel playback, and Android validation, while preserving the unresolved GitHub-to-Render SHA deployment proof gate.

## Constraints & Preferences
- Do not redesign approved application layout; prioritize stability, loading behavior, media lifecycle, uploads, Reels, and physical Android evidence.
- Do not claim `VERIFIED`, 10/10 autonomous status, Rork equivalence, deployment completion, or physical-device PASS without actual evidence.
- Production truth remains GitHub `main`, `https://api.ivxholding.com/version`, and `https://api.ivxholding.com/health`.
- Do not expose, use, log, rotate, or replace credential values or the previously exposed Render deploy-hook URL.
- Do not rely on in-app “certified/live” messages when SHA evidence contradicts them.
- Do not claim Instagram proprietary implementation; use only general perceived-performance and media-lifecycle practices.
- User explicitly requested Android APK generation, install, and physical Android soak testing; an Android Kotlin app was created at `android-ivx-holdings/`.

## Progress
### Done
- Verified the prior production mismatch:
  - Public GitHub `main`: `edf62a9f4940fb85d9b1b49406608b955861094d`
  - Production `/version`: `905ebdc996c0310528d417d8a387f1111023eeb1`
  - Production `/health`: healthy; runtime evidence previously reported `905ebdc…`.
- Identified Render build blocker:
  - `backend/services/ivx-ses-email.ts: Unexpected end of file`
  - GitHub raw `backend/services/ivx-ses-email.ts` at `edf62a9…` is Base64-like source rather than valid TypeScript.
- Repaired workspace `backend/services/ivx-ses-email.ts` as plain TypeScript.
- Validated repaired SES module:
  - `bun build "backend/services/ivx-ses-email.ts" --target=node --format=esm --outfile=/dev/null`
  - Result: `Bundled 1 module`.
  - Dynamic import smoke test passed: `{"moduleLoaded":true,"isSesConfiguredType":"boolean","exportCount":7}`.
- Added live commit equality as an IVX senior-developer completion condition in `backend/services/ivx-senior-developer-runtime.ts`:
  - `liveCommitVerification: IVXLiveCommitMatchResult`
  - `endToEndProductionComplete` now requires requested GitHub SHA to match live runtime SHA.
- Ran live-commit proof tests:
  - `bun test "backend/verify-live-commit-match.test.ts"`
  - Result: `6 pass`, `0 fail`, `27 expect() calls`.
- Audited existing Expo implementation:
  - Root singleton React Query client exists in `expo/app/_layout.tsx`.
  - Existing Reel lifecycle implementation exists in `expo/app/videos.tsx`, `expo/hooks/useReelPlayback.ts`, and `expo/components/SafeVideo.tsx`.
  - Existing Reel feed hook advertises cursor pagination and ID deduplication in `expo/hooks/useReelsFeed.ts`.
  - Existing backend feed and presigned upload routes exist in `backend/api/ivx-video-platform.ts`.
- Created Kotlin Android project `android-ivx-holdings/` after explicit Android request.
- Added unvalidated Android foundation files:
  - Cache-first feed repository and `FeedViewModel`.
  - Single-player `ReelPlaybackCoordinator` using Media3.
  - WorkManager-backed streaming upload queue with persistent URI, idempotency key, checksum generation, retry constraints, and stage persistence.
  - Compose `ReelsScreen`, `UploadScreen`, and cache-first `HomeScreen`.
  - Navigation routes for `home`, `reels`, and `upload`.
  - Media3 HLS/ExoPlayer and WorkManager Gradle dependencies.
- Started Android icon generation:
  - Generation ID: `dzuyj1ta2mbcavn22b9fj`.
- Updated the active priority statement in `.rork/plans/ivx-ia-final-certification-terminal-stat_1784657316341.plan.md` to the P0 media/reels stability program.

### In Progress
- Android Kotlin additions need compilation, dependency resolution, runtime testing, and integration review.
- Android icon generation is pending completion.
- Existing Expo app still needs the requested comprehensive module-by-module loading, caching, upload, realtime, and Reels audit; no end-to-end remediation has been proven there.
- Workspace SES repair still has not reached public GitHub as a new SHA.
- Awaiting Render Auto-Deploy for a corrected new GitHub SHA and final three-way SHA verification.

### Blocked
- Render cannot build `edf62a9…` because GitHub stores `backend/services/ivx-ses-email.ts` as Base64 text, producing `Unexpected end of file`.
- Re-deploying `edf62a9…` will reproduce the same failure.
- No verified GitHub push, Render deployment ID, new runtime SHA, APK artifact, physical Android device, physical Android soak run, iOS infrastructure, crash logs, or performance metrics are available.
- Full TypeScript validation remains unavailable in this workspace:
  - `bunx tsc --noEmit --pretty false`
  - `Cannot find type definition file for 'bun'.`
  - `Cannot find type definition file for 'node'.`
- New Android upload worker is only a client foundation:
  - It calls `POST /api/ivx/video-platform/admin/upload`, but server-side session reconciliation, multipart/resume semantics, checksum verification, processing polling, and publish confirmation are not yet verified.
- The Android native project is separate from existing `expo/` mobile implementation; creating it does not prove the current production APK contains the Kotlin changes.

## Key Decisions
- Do not manually redeploy `edf62a9f4940fb85d9b1b49406608b955861094d`; commit corrected plain TypeScript as a new SHA first.
- Keep Render Auto-Deploy configured as `On Commit` for `main`; the corrected new SHA should trigger the deployment.
- Treat `verifyLiveCommitMatch` as the required release-proof gate: requested commit must equal the live `/version` or fallback health commit.
- Use cache-first UI behavior: cached content remains visible during background refresh; only no-cache states receive skeleton/loading UI.
- Use one active Android Media3 `ExoPlayer` via `ReelPlaybackCoordinator`, not one player per Reel card.
- Limit Android Reel pager precomposition to active ±1 via `beyondViewportPageCount = 1`; distant pages should be poster-only.
- Use WorkManager and persistent content URI permission for Android upload work so queued uploads can survive navigation/process restart where platform permits.
- Do not publish uploaded media based solely on client upload completion; server processing must mark media ready before feed publication.
- Do not mark any current outcome `VERIFIED`; current state is partial implementation and unverified deployment/device validation.

## Next Steps
- 1. Inspect and correct compile issues in `android-ivx-holdings/`, then run its Gradle build and Android tests.
- 2. Wait for and install icon generation result `dzuyj1ta2mbcavn22b9fj`.
- 3. Audit all existing Expo screens/modules against the requested inventory, documenting actual screen files, query hooks, routes, database sources, cache keys, loading/error UI, pagination, refresh, realtime, media, and observed defects.
- 4. Consolidate Expo query defaults, keys, cache persistence, cancellation, pagination, optimistic updates, error normalization, and offline behavior without adding per-component query clients.
- 5. Upgrade existing Expo upload paths into one canonical persistent state machine covering posts, Reels, deal media, profile images, documents, and message attachments.
- 6. Instrument existing Expo Reel crashes and playback lifecycle before making broad player changes; capture device/app/SHA/media/player/memory/network/trace metadata.
- 7. Implement and test server-side upload reconciliation, processing-status polling, ready-only publication, media variants, canonical media IDs, and scoped cache invalidation.
- 8. Add automated tests for cache behavior, pagination/deduplication, media association, upload stages, signed URL recovery, playback coordinator lifecycle, error boundaries, network recovery, and realtime cleanup.
- 9. Commit `backend/services/ivx-ses-email.ts` repair and other validated changes to `ibb142/rork-global-real-estate-invest` as a new GitHub SHA.
- 10. Confirm Render Auto-Deploy for that new SHA; capture deployment ID and logs if it fails.
- 11. Verify GitHub `main` SHA equals `/version` `.commit` equals `/health` `.commit`, with `/health.ok === true`.
- 12. Build a new production Android APK with incremented version code, obtain its URL/SHA-256, install it on a real Android device, and execute the specified 100-swipe/15-minute/upload/network soak matrix.
- 13. Repeat relevant checks on physical iOS only when real iOS infrastructure is available.

- Current verified mismatch:
  - GitHub: `edf62a9f4940fb85d9b1b49406608b955861094d`
  - Live: `905ebdc996c0310528d417d8a387f1111023eeb1`
- Live `/version` previously returned:
  - `commitShort`: `905ebdc9`
  - `deploymentMarker`: `ivx-owner-ai-hono-autodeploy-live (see commit+bootTime for freshness)`.
- Render configuration in `render.yaml`:
  - Service: `ivx-holdings-platform`
  - Branch: `main`
  - Runtime: `docker`
  - Docker command: `node /app/node_modules/tsx/dist/cli.mjs /app/server.ts`
  - `autoDeployTrigger: commit`
  - Health path: `/health`.
- Root cause of failed deployment is source representation, not repository disconnection:
  - Raw GitHub `backend/services/ivx-ses-email.ts` is encoded content.
  - Render parses raw `.ts` and fails before startup.
- Existing production health output reported configured production-side GitHub/Render credentials and capability; sandbox credential absence does not prove production credentials are absent.
- Existing Expo Reels implementation already claims:
  - only one active Reel,
  - mounted active ±1,
  - app/focus pause behavior,
  - 80% visibility threshold,
  - per-item error containment.
  These claims require physical-device verification; they are not acceptance evidence.
- Existing backend upload endpoint is `POST /api/ivx/video-platform/admin/upload`; source comments state it returns `{ ok, uploadUrl, videoId, thumbnailUrl?, key }`.
- Android additions have not been built or run. Potential implementation concerns to resolve before relying on them include API authentication, correct feed response shape, upload session contract, server publish/reconciliation contract, WorkManager progress reporting, cancellation persistence, and robust media metadata validation.
- No proof exists for:
  - 100 consecutive physical Android Reel swipes,
  - 15-minute Reel soak,
  - real Android upload interruption/restart recovery,
  - APK SHA-256,
  - Android memory/FPS/ANR/crash metrics,
  - current APK source SHA,
  - iOS testing.
- “Same level as Rork” and “10/10 senior developer” remain unverified claims until deployment and full acceptance gates pass.

# Query Retries

When a `useQuery` query fails (the query function throws an error), TanStack Query will automatically retry the query if that query's request has not reached the max number of consecutive retries (defaults to `3`) or a function is provided to determine if a retry is allowed.

You can configure retries both on a global level and an individual query level.

- Setting `retry = false` will disable retries.
- Setting `retry = 6` will retry failing requests 6 times before showing the final error thrown by the function.
- Setting `retry = true` will infinitely retry failing requests.
- Setting `retry = (failureCount, error) => ...` allows for custom logic based on why the request failed.

```tsx
import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query'

// Make a specific query retry a certain number of times
const result = useQuery({
  queryKey: ['todos', 1],
  queryFn: fetchTodoListPage,
  retry: 10, // Will retry failed requests 10 times before displaying an error
})

```

## Retry Delay

By default, retries in TanStack Query do not happen immediately after a request fails. As is standard, a back-off delay is gradually applied to each retry attempt.

The default `retryDelay` is set to double (starting at `1000` ms) with each attempt, but not exceed 30 seconds:

```tsx
// Configure for all queries
import {
  QueryCache,
  QueryClient,
  QueryClientProvider,
} from '@tanstack/react-query'

const queryClient = new QueryClient({
  defaultOptions: {
    queries: {
      retryDelay: (attemptIndex) => Math.min(1000 * 2 ** attemptIndex, 30000),
    },
  },
})

function App() {
  return <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>...</QueryClientProvider>
}

```

Though it is not recommended, you can obviously override the `retryDelay` function/integer in both the Provider and individual query options. If set to an integer instead of a function the delay will always be the same amount of time:

```tsx
const result = useQuery({
  queryKey: ['todos'],
  queryFn: fetchTodoList,
  retryDelay: 1000, // Will always wait 1000ms to retry, regardless of how many retries
})

```
